name: Window Splitter
description: A moveable separator between two panes allowing users to adjust relative size of each pane; can be variable or fixed (toggling between two positions).

keyboard_interactions.action: Moves a vertical splitter to the left
Moves a vertical splitter to the right
(Optional) Sets primary pane to minimum size
(Optional) Sets primary pane to maximum size

notes: A focusable separator (role='separator' with tabindex='0') is a WIDGET. A decorative <hr> is role='separator' too but is NOT focusable and takes no value — do not confuse them.

RAWeb 13.10.2: dragging is path-based. You must offer a single-pointer alternative — a double-click to reset to default, or collapse/expand buttons. A keyboard alternative does NOT satisfy 13.10, which is specifically about pointer operation.
aria-valuenow is the primary pane's size as a percentage. aria-valuemin/max are its allowed bounds.
aria-controls must reference the PRIMARY pane — the one whose size aria-valuenow describes.
aria-valuetext makes the announcement comprehensible: 'Sidebar 30% of width' beats '30'.
Enter should toggle collapse and restore the previous size — a genuinely useful shortcut that is also a single-point-friendly affordance.
The splitter needs a hit area of at least 24px even if it renders as a 1px line, or it is untargetable for anyone with a tremor.
Ask whether you need it at all. A resizable pane is a convenience; consider whether fixed or user-preference-persisted widths would do.

raweb_criteria.reason: role='separator' with aria-valuenow/min/max must be exposed, plus aria-controls naming the pane it resizes.
Arrow keys must move the splitter; Enter must toggle collapse.
The splitter is a thin line — its focus indicator needs particular care.

Test 13.10.2 — dragging a splitter is a PATH-BASED gesture. The same resize must be achievable with a single-point operation: a double-click to reset, or explicit collapse/expand buttons. Keyboard support does not satisfy this criterion; it is about pointer users.
The resize must commit on pointer release and be abortable mid-drag.
